title: Five Ways That AI Front-Runners Change How Work Gets Done
gist: A BCG Institute study of 50+ AI front-runner companies finds that redesigning work and talent around AI (not just layering AI tools on old processes) drives 11+ percentage points of annual industry-adjusted shareholder-return outperformance, achieved through five consistent shifts: outcome ownership over assigned tasks, AI-produces/human-directs work with new role archetypes, reversibility-based decision rights, consequential rather than routine meetings, and judgment/impact-based compensation.

themes.theme: The performance stakes and study scope

insights.claim: Companies that redesign work and talent around AI, rather than layering AI tools on old approaches, outperform peers by more than 11 percentage points in industry-adjusted shareholder returns annually, driven by revenue growth and margin expansion.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: An 11-point annual TSR gap is a large, quantified incentive for boards to treat AI-driven operating-model redesign as a strategic priority rather than a cost-cutting IT project, since the reward for doing it right is a real market-return premium.
insights.quote: companies that are able to make this transformation... outperform their peers by more than 11 percentage points in industry-adjusted shareholder returns annually, driven by revenue growth and margin expansion
insights.locator: A recent BCG Institute study showed

insights.claim: The study is based on interviews with senior leaders at more than 50 AI front-runner firms across ten countries and a dozen-plus industries, split into 23 AI-native companies, 18 digital platforms with AI as core engine, and 9 incumbents rewiring functions around AI.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: The sample composition (skewed toward AI-native and digital-first firms) is important context for judging how directly the findings transfer to traditional incumbents, which made up under a fifth of the sample.
insights.quote: we went to the source, interviewing senior leaders at more than 50 AI front-runner firms... including 23 AI natives built on AI, 18 digital platforms with AI as the core engine, and 9 incumbent enterprises
insights.locator: To better understand this journey in practice

insights.claim: Five behavioral dimensions recurred consistently across the interview sample regardless of company size, geography, or archetype, and 80% of companies studied demonstrated at least three of the five.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: The 80%-showing-at-least-three-of-five statistic suggests these dimensions function as a coherent package rather than independent options, implying companies attempting only one or two shifts may be missing the combined effect that drives the performance gap.
insights.quote: Five held up consistently, and became the dimensions described here... 80% of companies demonstrated at least three of the five

themes.theme: Purpose of work: from assigned jobs to owned outcomes

insights.claim: In more than half of the AI front-runner sample, leadership sets direction but individuals and teams own the outcomes, with employees accountable for the 'what' but given latitude on the 'how,' and roles blurring so people assemble around problems rather than org-chart positions.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: Majority adoption of outcome-ownership over task-assignment is a structural signal that rigid job-description-based org design is becoming a competitive liability in AI-intensive industries.
insights.quote: in more than half of our sample of AI front-runners, leadership sets the direction, but individuals and teams own the outcomes
insights.locator: The Purpose of Work: From Assigned Jobs

insights.claim: Just under two-thirds of leaders interviewed said their company heavily reduced procedural checks and signoffs, replacing upfront approvals with after-action reviews, staged rollouts, and broad team access instead of weekly status reviews.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: A roughly two-thirds shift away from signoff-based control toward after-action review is a concrete, measurable governance change that traditional companies can benchmark themselves against when assessing how far behind front-runners they are.
insights.quote: just under two-thirds of the leaders we spoke to noted their company had heavily reduced procedural checks and signoffs, instead putting real tools and budgets in people’s hands
insights.locator: In fact, just under two-thirds of the leaders

themes.theme: The work itself: AI produces, humans direct and evaluate

insights.claim: In AI front-runner firms, work shifts from executing tasks to framing problems and setting objectives: AI does more of the drafting/building/executing while people direct, steer, and evaluate whether output is good enough to ship, letting one person cover work that used to take a team.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: If one person can now cover what previously took a team, this directly implies smaller, higher-leverage headcount structures become the norm in AI-intensive functions, changing how organizations should plan hiring and span of control.
insights.quote: AI handles more of the doing (drafting, building, executing) and people shift to directing the technology... One person can now produce what used to take a team

insights.claim: Two-thirds of interviewees described purposefully training their workforce to direct AI (not just use it), through explicit AI-fluency expectations, hiring for AI competence, and continuous peer-led learning.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: A two-thirds prevalence of deliberate AI-fluency programs (versus passive tool rollout) suggests that simply giving employees AI tools without a structured fluency program is already a below-median practice among front-runners.
insights.quote: two-thirds describe purposefully training up their workforce so more people can direct AI, not just use it

insights.claim: Zapier defines AI fluency across four dimensions — mindset (curiosity), strategy (matching problem to tool), building (hands-on quality output), and accountability (holding output to a goal) — treating it as how a person thinks about their thinking, not mere tool use.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: This four-dimension fluency framework is a reusable rubric other organizations can directly adopt for hiring, evaluation, and development criteria rather than inventing their own AI-competence definition from scratch.
insights.quote: Zapier defines AI fluency across four dimensions—mindset (curiosity), strategy... building... and accountability

themes.theme: Five new role archetypes for the AI operating model

insights.claim: Citizen Builders are non-engineering operators who build their own apps and agents, reducing dependency on engineering or outside agencies; at Cursor, an internal marketer built an app that replaced an entire agency, and at DevRev a sales-ops person with no technical background built a production Slack bot integrated with the CRM.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: Non-technical staff replacing agency spend or building production tools themselves is a direct cost and vendor-dependency reduction lever that any company with underused domain staff and accessible AI tooling could replicate.
insights.quote: An internal marketer replaced an entire agency by building an app that generated thousands of growth-marketing assets... a sales-ops person with no technical background built a full Slack bot that reads from and writes back to the CRM

insights.claim: Workflow Designers rethink multistep internal processes end-to-end, deciding what AI absorbs versus what stays human; at Writer, redesigning the workflow let AI mine sales calls for customer questions while humans focused on judgment-based content decisions, and Greenhouse created a dedicated 'innovation lead' role per department to identify and automate workflows.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: A dedicated role tasked with redrawing human/AI handoff points (rather than leaving this to ad hoc adoption) is a concrete organizational design pattern that traditional companies can install as a first step in AI transformation.
insights.quote: People in this role rethink a company’s internal multistep processes from end to end: mapping how work flows across people today, deciding what AI should absorb versus what stays human

insights.claim: AI Guardians govern risk and compliance for AI systems; one company runs a dedicated AI council that reviews and votes on proposed AI use cases before rollout, and Scale AI maintains a unit that systematically attacks its own models to test guardrails against hallucination and data leakage.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: A formal AI-council gating process before deployment, plus active red-teaming of one's own systems, is a governance pattern that risk and compliance teams elsewhere can adopt to reduce hallucination and data-leakage exposure before it becomes a public incident.
insights.quote: Scale AI maintains a dedicated unit to strengthen the guardrails of the firm’s own models and agentic systems against hallucinations and data leakage by subjecting them to systematic attack

insights.claim: Domain Anchors encode expert knowledge into reusable form so the whole organization can use it, not just people near the expert; four in five firms studied described doing this, and at Reserv, agent-captured expertise cut L&D program build time from 18 months to four weeks and regulatory-change response time from about three days to about an hour.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: An 18-months-to-4-weeks and 3-days-to-1-hour compression from encoding expert knowledge into reusable agents is a striking, specific ROI case for knowledge-capture investments, giving a concrete magnitude to expect from similar domain-anchor initiatives.
insights.quote: The time to build a new learning-and-development program fell from 18 months to four weeks, responses to regulatory changes dropped from about three days to about an hour
insights.locator: Insurtech company Reserv built its own platform

insights.claim: Agent Shepherds oversee how a fleet of AI agents operate, including access control, hosting, and shutting down misbehaving agents, as at Bolt.new's central AI-native governance role and Walmart's orchestration roles managing its marketplace of customer-facing and internal super-agents.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: As agent fleets scale, a dedicated oversight role for access control and shutdown authority becomes a necessary operational control, not optional governance overhead, especially for firms deploying customer-facing agents at Walmart's scale.
insights.quote: Walmart is creating orchestration roles to manage its complex, interconnected AI systems—an extensive marketplace of agents spanning customer-facing and internal super-agents

themes.theme: Decision architecture: from concentrated to distributed

insights.claim: AI front-runners tie decision rights to the reversibility of a call rather than seniority: deterministic rule-based calls go to agents, reversible low-risk calls move to whoever is closest to the work, and irreversible calls stay with senior leaders, with accountability dispersed accordingly.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: Reversibility-based decision routing is a directly implementable governance rule that any organization can apply immediately to decide which decisions to push down or automate, independent of broader cultural change.
insights.quote: Decision rights are tied to the reversibility of the call, rather than seniority level, while accountability is more broadly dispersed.

insights.claim: At Jellyfish, automating repetitive integration code let the engineer who writes a change approve it directly rather than requiring code-owner signoff, cutting review time for changes from three days to within a day; about half of firms interviewed described pushing decisions downward this way.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: A 3x reduction in change-clearance time from removing a signoff bottleneck quantifies the throughput cost of centralized approval structures, a concrete case for reviewing similar signoff gates elsewhere.
insights.quote: Today, the engineer who writes the change approves it, minding guardrails agreed once rather than a review each time, and changes clear within a day rather than three.

insights.claim: More than half of firms interviewed described deliberately building employee judgment to support pushed-down decisions, by making reasoning visible in open channels, normalizing challenge and discussion, and giving less-experienced employees real decisions earlier with senior support.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: This flags that distributed decision-making only works if paired with deliberate judgment-building; pushing decisions down without this investment risks worse outcomes, a caution for companies tempted to decentralize decisions purely for speed.
insights.quote: pushing decisions down works only if people have the judgment to make them. More than half the firms we spoke to described building this judgment deliberately
insights.locator: Of course, pushing decisions down works

themes.theme: Coordination of work: fewer routine syncs, more consequential meetings

insights.claim: About two-thirds of interviewees said meetings have become more consequential as AI absorbs routine admin and alignment tasks, with a majority describing middle managers shifting from coordinators to player-coaches.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: A shift of middle managers from coordination to player-coach roles implies headcount and job-description changes for middle management specifically, a segment often assumed to be most exposed to AI-driven redundancy rather than role transformation.
insights.quote: About two-thirds of our interviewees said meetings have become more consequential, and a majority described middle managers shifting from being coordinators to become player-coaches.
insights.locator: The Coordination of Work: From Routine

insights.claim: DevRev spent two years building a proprietary company-wide knowledge system (Computer) that any employee can query directly for answers, removing information handoffs that normally run through the management hierarchy.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: A two-year build timeline for a company-wide queryable knowledge system is a realistic cost/time benchmark for organizations considering a similar internal-knowledge infrastructure investment.
insights.quote: DevRev spent two years building a proprietary knowledge system, Computer, that holds company-wide context centrally.

themes.theme: Rewards and compensation: judgment and impact over tenure and activity

insights.claim: About three-quarters of AI front-runners weigh judgment over activity when evaluating success, testing people in real time by asking them to explain their plan before work starts and to show where they overrode the AI's output.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: A three-quarters prevalence of judgment-over-activity evaluation is a strong signal that traditional output-volume-based performance metrics are becoming obsolete in AI-intensive workplaces and should be redesigned proactively rather than reactively.
insights.quote: Some three-quarters weigh judgment over activity. So the test moves off the page and into real time: people are asked to explain their plan before work starts and to show where they overrode what the AI gave them.
insights.locator: When evaluating success, AI front-runners focus

insights.claim: Zapier evaluates people on impact rather than activity because AI is 'brilliant at activity,' meaning a worker can rack up heavy tool usage yet accomplish nothing of value.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: This directly warns against using AI-usage volume as a performance proxy, a mistake companies rushing to measure 'AI adoption' internally are prone to making.
insights.quote: Zapier evaluates people on impact, not activity... it notes that AI is brilliant at activity, so someone can rack up heavy tool usage yet accomplish nothing.

insights.claim: By making knowledge-sharing a visible path to career success rather than a threat to indispensability, front-runner firms like Writer counter the traditional incentive for experts to hoard knowledge for job security.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: This identifies a specific, fixable incentive misalignment (expert hoarding for job security) that undermines AI-driven knowledge capture unless recognition systems are explicitly redesigned to reward sharing.
insights.quote: In traditional firms, experts are often disincentivized to pass on their knowledge for fear of losing their status as ‘indispensable.’ By making the act of sharing knowledge a visible path to success, AI front-runners ensure it's more widely dispersed

themes.theme: Roadmap and sequencing for traditional companies

insights.claim: Among large companies in the study, new AI-era roles and judgment-based evaluation are the dimensions adopted fastest (because they don't require dismantling anything), while redefining work around outcomes is underway at only about two-thirds of large companies and fewer than half have pushed decision authority down the hierarchy.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: This ranks the five dimensions by adoption difficulty for incumbents, giving traditional-company leaders a realistic sequencing guide: expect roles and judgment-based evaluation to be achievable first, and decision-rights redistribution to be the hardest and slowest change.
insights.quote: Roles and judgment shift fastest... redefining work around outcomes is underway at only about two-thirds of large companies, and fewer than half have pushed authority down the corporate hierarchy.
insights.locator: Leaders have pushed further and faster

insights.claim: BCG recommends traditional companies sequence AI transformation in three stages: build the foundation (define value, define AI fluency, equip people), pick a beachhead function to prove the model, then scale role archetypes and rewire talent/performance processes enterprise-wide.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: This three-stage roadmap (foundation, beachhead, scale) is a directly actionable project-planning template for any incumbent CEO or CHRO starting an AI-driven operating-model redesign, rather than a vague call to 'transform.'
insights.quote: What follows is a roadmap that traditional companies should keep in mind... first building the foundation, then proving it in one place, and finally scaling it across the enterprise.

insights.claim: Rivian's software division ran its own AI framework roughly six months ahead of the rest of the business as a deliberate 'beachhead,' and now serves as the internal reference point as the company extends the model outward.
insights.speaker: Sagar Goel
insights.so_what: A six-month head-start beachhead approach at Rivian is a concrete, time-boxed example of the pilot-then-scale sequencing BCG recommends, useful as a benchmark timeline for other companies planning their own pilot phase.
insights.quote: Rivian’s software division moved first and furthest, running its own AI framework about half a year ahead of the rest of the business.
